steps.practice: Compile Hello.java, find the Hello.class file it made, then run it with 'java Hello'.
steps.detail: javac checks your code and writes a .class file of bytecode. The java command starts the Java Virtual Machine, which runs that bytecode. You give java the class name, not the file name. Because every system has its own JVM, the same .class file runs anywhere.
steps.proof: A Hello.class file appears, and 'java Hello' prints the message.
steps.pitfall: Running 'java Hello.class', which looks for a class literally named Hello.class.

problems.prompt: What file does 'javac Hello.java' create?
Do you type 'java Hello.class' or 'java Hello' to run it?
Why can 1 .class file run on both Windows and Mac?
problems.answer: Each system's JVM runs the same bytecode.

steps.title: Read Compiler Errors
steps.mastery: Read a compiler error's file, line number and message, and fix the first error first.
steps.practice: Delete a semicolon and misspell 'String' in Hello.java, compile, and fix the errors in the order they're reported.
steps.detail: Each error names the file and line, then a short message. Errors cascade: one missing brace can cause a dozen later complaints. So fix the first one, recompile, and see what's left. If the line looks fine, check the end of the line above it.
steps.proof: Both errors fixed, and the program compiles and runs.
steps.pitfall: Fixing errors from the bottom of the list up.

problems.prompt: javac says 'Hello.java:5: error: ';' expected'. Which line do you check?
problems.answer: 5, or the end of the line before it.

problems.prompt: javac reports 12 errors after you deleted 1 brace. Which do you fix first?
problems.answer: The first one. The rest often vanish.

problems.prompt: What does 'cannot find symbol: variable totl' mean?
problems.answer: You used a name that was never declared, likely a typo.

steps.title: Use an IDE
steps.mastery: Set up an IDE like IntelliJ or VS Code for Java, and run and debug a class from it.
steps.practice: Open Hello.java in IntelliJ IDEA, run it with the green arrow, then set 1 breakpoint and step through it.
steps.detail: An IDE compiles as you type, underlines errors, suggests fixes and runs the debugger with a click. It saves time, but practice writing some code by hand too, because the AP exam is on paper with no autocomplete.
steps.proof: The program runs from the IDE, and the debugger stops on the breakpoint.
steps.pitfall: Relying so much on autocomplete that you can't write a for loop from memory.

problems.prompt: Name 1 free IDE that runs Java.
problems.answer: IntelliJ IDEA Community, Eclipse or VS Code.

problems.prompt: A red underline appears under 'Sytem.out'. What's wrong?
Why does the AP exam have you write Java without an IDE?
problems.answer: It tests whether you know the syntax without autocomplete.

steps.title: Compare With .equals
steps.mastery: Compare strings with .equals, and explain why == compares references instead.
steps.practice: Create String a = "hi" and String b = new String("hi"), print a == b and a.equals(b), and explain the difference.
steps.detail: A String variable holds a reference to an object. == asks whether two references point at the same object. .equals asks whether the characters match. Two separate String objects with the same text are equal by .equals but not by ==, which is the classic AP trap.
steps.proof: a == b prints false and a.equals(b) prints true.
steps.pitfall: Using == to compare user input with a word, which can fail even when the text matches.

problems.prompt: String a = new String("cat"); String b = new String("cat"); What does a.equals(b) give?
For those same 2 strings, what does a == b give?
Write the condition that checks whether name holds "Ana", ignoring case.

steps.title: Length, charAt and substring
steps.mastery: Use the String methods length(), charAt() and substring(), with indexes that start at 0.
steps.practice: For s = "computer", find s.length(), s.charAt(3), s.substring(2, 5) and s.substring(4).
steps.detail: Indexes run from 0 to length() - 1. substring(a, b) starts at a and stops before b, so its length is b - a. substring(a) runs to the end. An index out of range throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.
steps.proof: 8, 'p', "mpu" and "uter".
steps.pitfall: Thinking substring(2, 5) includes the character at index 5.

problems.prompt: What is "java".length()?
What is "hello".charAt(1)?
What is "science".substring(1, 4)?

steps.title: Search With indexOf
steps.mastery: Find text with indexOf, which returns -1 when the text isn't there.
steps.practice: For s = "banana", find s.indexOf("a"), s.indexOf("na"), s.indexOf("z") and s.indexOf("a", 2).
steps.detail: indexOf returns the position of the first match. A second argument says where to start looking. If there's no match, it returns -1, so checking indexOf(x) != -1 is a quick contains test. There's also lastIndexOf for the final match.
steps.pitfall: Treating 0 as not found. 0 means it was found at the very start.

problems.prompt: What is "mississippi".indexOf("ss")?
What is "apple".indexOf("q")?
Write a condition that's true when word contains the letter 'x'.

steps.title: Strings Don't Change
steps.mastery: Remember that String methods return new strings, so you have to save the result.
steps.practice: Run String s = "hi"; s.toUpperCase(); System.out.println(s); then explain what prints and fix it.
steps.detail: Strings are immutable: no method changes the original. toUpperCase, substring and replace all hand back a new string. If you don't assign it to something, it's thrown away. Also, + with a String turns everything after it into text, left to right.
steps.proof: It prints hi. The fix is s = s.toUpperCase();.
steps.pitfall: Calling a String method on its own line and expecting the variable to change.

problems.prompt: String s = "abc"; s.toUpperCase(); What is s now?
Write the line that makes s hold "ABC" from "abc".
String t = "a" + 1 + 2; What is t?

steps.title: Loop Over Strings
steps.mastery: Loop over a string's characters to count, reverse or build a new string.
steps.practice: Write a loop that counts the vowels in "education", and another that builds its reverse.
steps.detail: Loop i from 0 to length() - 1 and use charAt(i) or substring(i, i + 1). To count, add to a counter when the character matches. To build, start with an empty string and add each piece. Adding to the front reverses, and adding to the back copies.
steps.proof: 5 vowels, and "noitacude".
steps.pitfall: Using i <= s.length(), which runs one step too far and crashes.

problems.prompt: How many times does 'for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++)' run when s is "loop"?
A loop adds each s.charAt(i) to the front of an empty r, for s = "abc". What is r?
What is 3 + 2 + "5" in Java?

steps.title: The Main Primitives
steps.mastery: Choose between int, double, boolean and char for a value, and declare it.
steps.practice: Declare 4 variables, a count, a price, a flag and a grade letter, each with the right primitive type.
steps.detail: int holds whole numbers, double holds decimals, boolean holds true or false, and char holds one character in single quotes. Java checks types when it compiles, so putting 3.5 into an int is an error rather than a silent bug.
steps.proof: Use int count = 0, double price = 4.99, boolean done = false and char grade = 'A'.
steps.pitfall: Writing a char with double quotes. "A" is a String.

problems.prompt: Which type holds 3.75: int or double?
Which literal is a char: 'A' or "A"?
What type is the literal 'true'?

steps.title: Integer Division
steps.mastery: Predict integer division and the % remainder in Java.
steps.practice: Evaluate 17 / 5, 17 % 5, 17.0 / 5 and -17 / 5 in Java, and explain each one.
steps.detail: When both sides of / are ints, Java drops the decimal part, truncating toward zero. If either side is a double, you get a double. % gives the remainder and keeps the sign of the left side. This trips up more AP students than almost anything else.
steps.pitfall: Expecting -17 / 5 to be -4. Java truncates toward zero, so it's -3.

problems.prompt: What is 7 / 2 in Java?
What is 7 / 2.0 in Java?
What is -7 / 2 in Java?

steps.title: Cast Between Types
steps.mastery: Cast between int and double, and know that a cast to int cuts off the decimal.
steps.practice: Evaluate (int) 3.99, (double) 7 / 2, (double) (7 / 2) and (int) -2.7.
steps.detail: A cast applies only to what comes right after it. (double) 7 / 2 casts the 7 first, so the division is decimal. (double) (7 / 2) divides as ints first and casts the 3. Casting to int never rounds. To round, use (int) (x + 0.5) for positive x.
steps.pitfall: Expecting (int) 3.99 to round up to 4.

problems.prompt: What is (int) 9.8?
What is (double) 5 / 2?
What is (double) (5 / 2)?

steps.title: Overflow and Limits
steps.mastery: Know the range of int and what happens when a value overflows it.
steps.practice: Print Integer.MAX_VALUE, then add 1 to it and print the result.
steps.detail: An int holds about plus or minus 2.1 billion. Go past the top and it wraps around to the most negative value with no error. That's overflow. Use long for bigger whole numbers, and watch sums and products in loops.
steps.pitfall: Assuming Java will warn you when an int overflows.

problems.prompt: About how big is Integer.MAX_VALUE: 2 million or 2 billion?
What does Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1 give?
Which type should hold the number 5,000,000,000: int or long?

steps.title: Compound Assignment and Increment
steps.mastery: Predict the results of +=, -=, *=, %=, ++ and -- on a variable.
steps.practice: Trace int x = 5; x += 3; x *= 2; x--; and give x after each line.
steps.detail: x += 3 is short for x = x + 3, and the same goes for the other operators. x++ adds 1 and x-- subtracts 1. Trace these one line at a time and write each new value down, because doing several in your head is where mistakes creep in.
steps.proof: 8, then 16, then 15.
steps.pitfall: Reading x *= 2 + 1 as (x * 2) + 1. The right side is worked out first, so it's x * 3.

problems.prompt: int a = 10; a -= 4; What is a?
int n = 3; n++; n++; What is n?
int x = 7; x %= 3; What is x?

steps.title: Justify in Words
steps.mastery: Write the reason a calculus conclusion follows, in the form graders expect.
steps.practice: Write a 2 sentence justification for a relative max at x = 3 when f prime changes from + to -.
steps.detail: AP graders want the reason tied to the derivative: f prime changes from positive to negative at x = 3. A correct answer without it loses points.
steps.proof: f has a relative max at x = 3 because f prime changes from positive to negative there.
steps.pitfall: Writing only the answer with no reason.

problems.prompt: Justify f increasing on (1, 4) given f prime.
Justify concave up at \(x = 2\).
problems.answer: f double prime \((2) > 0\), or f prime is increasing there.

problems.prompt: Justify an inflection point at \(x = 5\).
problems.answer: f double prime changes sign at \(x = 5\).

steps.title: Calculator Rules
steps.mastery: Know what the AP calculator section allows and how to report decimals.
steps.practice: Solve 3 calculator active AP problems and report every decimal to 3 places.
steps.detail: The calculator may graph, find zeros, take numerical derivatives and evaluate integrals. Answers need 3 correct decimal places, so keep full precision until the end.
steps.proof: 3 problems with answers to 3 decimals.
steps.pitfall: Rounding early and losing the third decimal.

problems.prompt: How many decimal places does the AP exam expect?
Should you round intermediate values to 3 places?
Name 4 things the AP calculator is expected to do.
problems.answer: Graph, find zeros, compute numerical derivatives and evaluate integrals.

steps.title: Free Response Practice
steps.mastery: Complete AP free response questions under time.
steps.practice: Complete 2 AP Calculus free response questions in 30 minutes, then score them with the official rubric.
steps.detail: Each FRQ has 9 points across parts. Scoring yourself with the rubric shows exactly which justifications and units you miss.
steps.proof: 2 FRQs scored with notes on lost points.
steps.pitfall: Checking answers without reading the rubric.

problems.prompt: How many points is a typical AP Calculus FRQ worth?
About how many minutes per FRQ on the exam?
You got the answer but no justification. Likely score for that part?
problems.answer: Partial or 0 for the reasoning point.

steps.title: Multiple Choice Strategy
steps.mastery: Pace the multiple choice section and use answer choices.
steps.practice: Take 15 AP Calculus multiple choice questions in 30 minutes and mark which ones you checked by plugging in choices.
steps.detail: The multiple choice section rewards speed. Plugging answer choices back in, or estimating with a graph, often beats solving from scratch.
steps.proof: 15 questions done with a time per question.
steps.pitfall: Spending 6 minutes on 1 question while easy ones wait.

problems.prompt: Average time per question for 15 in 30 minutes?
A choice gives \(f(2) = 7\) and you can check \(f(2)\) quickly. Do it?
Is there a penalty for wrong answers on AP multiple choice?

steps.title: Final Review Plan
steps.mastery: Plan the last 4 weeks before the AP exam.
steps.practice: Write a 4 week plan with 2 full practice exams and topic review of your 3 weakest units.
steps.detail: Full exams build stamina and timing, and topic review fixes the units that cost the most points. Space them out.
steps.proof: A 4 week plan with 2 exams scheduled.
steps.pitfall: Only reviewing favorite topics.

problems.prompt: In a 4 week plan, how many full practice exams make sense?
Your weakest units are series, related rates and FTC. Which first?
problems.answer: The one with the most exam weight or most missed points.

problems.prompt: Should your last full practice exam be 1 day or about 5 days before the AP exam?
problems.answer: About 5 days before, so the last few days are for review, not a full rehearsal.

steps.title: Area Between Curves
steps.mastery: Integrate top minus bottom to find the area between 2 curves.
steps.practice: Find the area between y = x and y = x^2 from x = 0 to x = 1.
steps.detail: Sketch first to see which curve is on top. Find intersection points for the limits if they are not given.
steps.proof: Integral of (x - x^2) from 0 to 1 = 1/6.
steps.pitfall: Subtracting in the wrong order and getting a negative area.

problems.prompt: Where do \(y = x\) and \(y = x^{2}\) meet?
Area between \(y = 4\) and \(y = x^{2}\)?
Area between \(y = \sqrt{x}\) and \(y = x\) on [0, 1]?

steps.title: Disk Method
steps.mastery: Find a volume of revolution by stacking circular disks.
steps.practice: Find the volume when y = sqrt(x) on [0, 4] is rotated about the x axis.
steps.detail: Each slice is a disk with radius f(x), so the volume is the integral of pi f(x)^2. Sketch the radius on a typical slice.
steps.proof: pi times the integral of x from 0 to 4 = 8 pi.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting to square the radius.

problems.prompt: Rotate \(y = x\) on [0, 3] about the \(x\) axis. Volume?
Rotate \(y = 2\) on [0, 5] about the \(x\) axis. Volume?
Rotate \(y = x^{2}\) on [0, 1] about the \(x\) axis. Volume?

steps.title: Washer Method
steps.mastery: Subtract an inner disk when the region has a hole.
steps.practice: Spin the region between y = 2 and y = sqrt(x) on [0, 4] around the x axis and compute its volume.
steps.detail: Use pi(R^2 - r^2), with R the outer radius and r the inner. Square each radius before subtracting.
steps.proof: pi times the integral of (4 - x) from 0 to 4 = 8 pi.
steps.pitfall: Squaring the difference (R - r)^2 instead of R^2 - r^2.

problems.prompt: Outer radius 3, inner 1. Washer area?
Rotate the region between \(y = 2\) and \(y = 1\) on [0, 4] about the \(x\) axis. Volume?
Which is the outer radius for \(y = x\) and \(y = x^{2}\) on [0, 1]?

steps.title: Cross Sections
steps.mastery: Find volumes with known square or triangle cross sections.
steps.practice: A base is the region under y = 4 - x^2 above the x axis, with square cross sections. Find the volume.
steps.detail: Each slice has area s^2 where s is the slice length. Integrate that area across the base.
steps.proof: Integral of (4 - x^2)^2 from -2 to 2 = 512/15.
steps.pitfall: Rotating the region when the problem uses cross sections.

problems.prompt: Square cross section with side 3. Area?
Semicircle cross section with diameter 4. Area?
Equilateral triangle cross section with side s. Area?

steps.title: Shell Method
steps.mastery: Use cylindrical shells when rotating around a vertical axis.
steps.practice: Rotate y = x^2 on [0, 2] about the y axis using shells and find the volume.
steps.detail: A shell has volume 2 pi (radius)(height)(thickness). Shells avoid solving for x in terms of y.
steps.proof: 2 pi times the integral of x^3 from 0 to 2 = 8 pi.
steps.pitfall: Using the disk method in x when the axis is vertical.

problems.prompt: Rotating about the line \(x = - 1\), what is the shell radius at \(x = 3\)?
Rotate \(y = x\) on [0, 1] about the \(y\) axis. Volume?
Find the volume when the rectangle under \(y = 1\) for \(0 \le x \le 3\) spins around the \(y\) axis.
problems.answer: \(9\pi\), a cylinder of radius 3 and height 1.

steps.title: Three Conditions
steps.mastery: Check that f(a) exists, the limit exists and the 2 are equal.
steps.practice: Test f(x) = (x^2 - 1)/(x - 1) for continuity at x = 1 using all 3 conditions.
steps.detail: A function is continuous at a point only if it is defined there, has a limit there and the two match. A hole fails the first condition even when the limit exists.
steps.proof: f(1) is undefined, so f is not continuous at 1, though the limit is 2.
steps.pitfall: Calling a function continuous because its limit exists.

problems.prompt: Is \(f(x) = x^{2}\) continuous at \(x = 3\)?
\(f(x) = \frac{1}{x - 2}\). Where is it not continuous?
Define \(f(1)\) to make \(\frac{x^{2} - 1}{x - 1}\) continuous.

steps.title: Types of Breaks
steps.mastery: Name a discontinuity as a hole, a jump or an asymptote.
steps.practice: Classify the breaks of (x - 2)/(x^2 - 4), the floor function at 3 and 1/x at 0.
steps.detail: A hole can be patched by defining one value, a jump has 2 different side limits and an asymptote blows up. The type tells you whether the break can be fixed.
steps.proof: A hole at 2 (and an asymptote at -2), a jump at 3 and an asymptote at 0.
steps.pitfall: Calling every discontinuity an asymptote.

problems.prompt: What kind of break does \(\frac{x - 1}{x - 1}\) have at 1?
What kind of break does \(\frac{1}{x + 4}\) have at -4?
\(f(x) = 2\) for \(x < 0\) and 3 for \(x \ge 0\). Type of break at 0?

steps.title: Piecewise Continuity
steps.mastery: Choose a constant so the pieces of a function meet.
steps.practice: Find k so that f(x) = kx + 1 for x < 2 and x^2 for x >= 2 is continuous.
steps.detail: At the boundary, set the 2 pieces equal. That single equation fixes the constant, and then the function has no jump.
steps.pitfall: Matching the pieces at the wrong x value.

problems.prompt: Find a so \(ax = 6\) at \(x = 3\) matches \(2x\) there.
Find c so \(f(x) = x + c\) for \(x < 1\) and \(3x\) for \(x \ge 1\) is continuous.
Find k so \(kx^{2}\) for \(x \le 2\) and \(4x - 4\) for \(x > 2\) is continuous.

steps.title: Intermediate Value Theorem
steps.mastery: Use IVT to show a continuous function hits a value between its endpoints.
steps.practice: Show x^3 + x - 1 = 0 has a root between 0 and 1 using f(0) and f(1).
steps.detail: If f is continuous on [a, b] and f(a) and f(b) have opposite signs, f must cross 0 in between. IVT says a root exists, not where.
steps.proof: f(0) = -1 and f(1) = 1, so a root lies in (0, 1).
steps.pitfall: Using IVT on a function that is not continuous.

problems.prompt: \(f(1) = - 3\) and \(f(4) = 5\) for a continuous f. Must f equal 0 somewhere in [1, 4]?
Does \(\frac{1}{x}\) take every value between -1 and 1 on [-1, 1]?
problems.answer: No, it is not continuous at 0, so IVT does not apply.

problems.prompt: Show \(\cos x = x\) has a solution in [0, 1].

steps.title: Continuity of Common Functions
steps.mastery: Know where polynomials, roots, logs and fractions are continuous.
steps.practice: List the domain of continuity for x^5 - x, sqrt(x - 3), ln(x) and 1/(x^2 - 9).
steps.detail: Polynomials are continuous everywhere, roots and logs on their domains, and fractions except where the bottom is 0. This saves a full check every time.
steps.proof: All reals, x >= 3, x > 0, and all reals except 3 and -3.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting the domain restriction on a log or root.

problems.prompt: Where is \(\frac{1}{x - 5}\) continuous?
Where is \(\ln (x + 2)\) continuous?
Where is \(\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}\) continuous?

steps.title: Increasing and Decreasing
steps.mastery: Use the sign of f prime to find where a graph rises and falls.
steps.practice: Find where f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 is increasing and decreasing with a sign chart.
steps.detail: Critical points split the line into intervals. The sign of f prime on each tells rising or falling.
steps.proof: Increasing on (-inf, 0) and (2, inf), decreasing on (0, 2).
steps.pitfall: Testing f instead of f prime on each interval.

problems.prompt: Where is \(x^{2}\) increasing?
Where is \(-x^{2} + 4x\) decreasing?
Where is \(x^{3}\) increasing?

steps.title: Concavity
steps.mastery: Use f double prime to find where a graph bends up or down.
steps.practice: Find the concavity and inflection points of f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2.
steps.detail: f double prime positive means concave up, negative means concave down. An inflection point is where the concavity changes.
steps.proof: f double prime = 6x - 6. Concave down for x < 1, up for x > 1, inflection at (1, -2).
steps.pitfall: Calling every zero of f double prime an inflection point without checking a sign change.

problems.prompt: Concavity of \(x^{2}\)?
Inflection point of \(x^{3}\)?
Does \(x^{4}\) have an inflection point at 0?
problems.answer: No, it is concave up on both sides.

steps.title: Second Derivative Test
steps.mastery: Classify critical points with the sign of f double prime.
steps.practice: Classify the critical points of f(x) = 2x^3 - 9x^2 + 12x with the second derivative test.
steps.detail: At a critical point, f double prime > 0 gives a local min and < 0 gives a local max. If it is 0, the test says nothing.
steps.proof: x = 1 is a local max and x = 2 is a local min.
steps.pitfall: Using the test where f double prime = 0 and drawing a conclusion.

problems.prompt: f prime \((3) = 0\) and f double prime \((3) = - 2\). What is \(x = 3\)?
f prime \((1) = 0\) and f double prime \((1) = 5\)?
\(f(x) = x^{4}\) at 0. Does the second derivative test decide?

steps.title: Read f From f Prime
steps.mastery: Describe f from a graph of its derivative.
steps.practice: From a graph of f prime crossing 0 at x = -1 and x = 3, describe where f has extremes.
steps.detail: Where f prime crosses from + to -, f has a max. Where f prime has a max or min, f has an inflection point.
steps.proof: f has a local max at -1 and a local min at 3 if the signs go +, -, +.
steps.pitfall: Reading the f prime graph as if it were f.

problems.prompt: f prime is positive on (0, 4). What does f do?
f prime has a max at \(x = 2\). What does f have there?
f' goes from negative to positive at \(x = 1\). What is \(x = 1\) for f?

steps.title: Sketch a Full Graph
steps.mastery: Combine intercepts, asymptotes and derivatives into one sketch.
steps.practice: Sketch f(x) = x/(x^2 + 1) using its intercept, asymptote, extremes and concavity.
steps.detail: Gather facts first: intercepts, asymptotes, f prime and f double prime sign charts. Then the sketch draws itself.
steps.proof: Intercept (0, 0), asymptote y = 0, max at (1, 1/2), min at (-1, -1/2).
steps.pitfall: Plotting points without using the derivative information.

problems.prompt: Horizontal asymptote of \(\frac{x}{x^{2} + 1}\)?
Critical points of \(\frac{x}{x^{2} + 1}\)?
Is \(\frac{x}{x^{2} + 1}\) odd or even?

steps.title: Derivative From the Limit
steps.mastery: Compute a derivative straight from the limit definition.
steps.practice: Find f prime of x for f(x) = x^2 using the limit of (f(x + h) - f(x))/h as h goes to 0.
steps.detail: The definition is the slope of a secant line as the 2 points merge. Expand, cancel the h and then let h go to 0.
steps.proof: (2xh + h^2)/h = 2x + h, so the derivative is 2x.
steps.pitfall: Setting h = 0 before cancelling, which gives 0/0.

problems.prompt: Using the definition, find \(f'(x)\) for \(f(x) = x^{2} + 3x\).
problems.answer: \(2x + 3\). The difference quotient simplifies to \(2x + h + 3\), which goes to \(2x + 3\) as h goes to 0.

problems.prompt: Using the definition, derivative of \(f(x) = x^{2} + 1\) at \(x = 2\)?
Using the definition, derivative of \(f(x) = \frac{1}{x}\)?

steps.title: Power Rule
steps.mastery: Find the derivative of x^n as n x^(n - 1) for any power.
steps.practice: Differentiate x^5, 4x^3, sqrt(x) and 1/x^2 with the power rule.
steps.detail: Rewrite roots and fractions as powers first: sqrt(x) = x^(1/2) and 1/x^2 = x^(-2). Then bring the power down and subtract 1.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting to rewrite a root as a power before differentiating.

problems.prompt: Derivative of \(x^{7}\)?
Derivative of \(6x^{\frac{2}{3}}\)?
Derivative of \(\frac{3}{x^{4}}\)?

steps.title: Slope of a Tangent
steps.mastery: Use the derivative to find the tangent line at a point.
steps.practice: Find the tangent line to y = x^3 - 2x at x = 1.
steps.detail: The derivative gives the slope at the point, and the point itself comes from the function. Point-slope form finishes the line.
steps.pitfall: Using the function value as the slope.

problems.prompt: Slope of \(y = x^{2}\) at \(x = 3\)?
Tangent line to \(y = x^{2}\) at \(x = 1\)?
Where does \(y = x^{2} - 4x\) have a horizontal tangent?

steps.title: Derivative as a Rate
steps.mastery: Read a derivative as an instantaneous rate with units.
steps.practice: A tank holds V(t) = 200 - 3t^2 liters after t minutes. Find V prime of 4 and state its units.
steps.detail: The derivative tells how fast the quantity changes right now. Units are output units per input unit, which keeps answers meaningful.
steps.proof: -24 liters per minute.
steps.pitfall: Leaving off units or getting the sign of a decrease wrong.

problems.prompt: \(s(t) = 5t^{2}\) meters. Velocity at \(t = 2\) seconds?
\(C(x) = 0.5x^{2}\) dollars for \(x\) items. Marginal cost at \(x = 10\)?
\(P(t) = 1000 + 50t\) people after t years. Rate at \(t = 3\)?

steps.title: Where It Fails
steps.mastery: Spot points where a function has no derivative.
steps.practice: Decide where |x - 2|, x^(1/3) and a function with a jump at 1 fail to be differentiable.
steps.detail: Corners, vertical tangents and breaks have no single slope. Differentiable implies continuous, but continuous does not imply differentiable.
steps.proof: At x = 2 (corner), x = 0 (vertical tangent) and x = 1 (jump).
steps.pitfall: Assuming every continuous function has a derivative everywhere.

problems.prompt: Is |x| differentiable at 0?
Is \(x^{2}\) differentiable at 0?
Can a function be differentiable at \(x = 3\) but not continuous there?

steps.title: Check a Solution
steps.mastery: Verify a function solves a differential equation by substituting.
steps.practice: Check that y = 3e^(2x) solves dy/dx = 2y.
steps.detail: Differentiate the proposed solution and substitute it into both sides. If they match for every x, it is a solution.
steps.proof: dy/dx = 6e^(2x) = 2(3e^(2x)), so yes.
steps.pitfall: Checking only at 1 value of x.

problems.prompt: Does \(y = x^{2}\) solve \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x\)?
Does \(y = e^{-x}\) solve \(y\) prime + \(y = 0\)?
Find k so \(y = e^{kx}\) solves \(y\) prime = \(5y\).

steps.title: Separate Variables
steps.mastery: Solve dy/dx = g(x)h(y) by moving all y terms to one side.
steps.practice: Solve dy/dx = xy with y(0) = 2 by separation of variables.
steps.detail: Divide by h(y), multiply by dx, integrate both sides and solve for y. Use the initial condition to find the constant.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting the constant or adding it after solving for y.

problems.prompt: Solve \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 3y\) with \(y(0) = 1\).
Solve \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x}{y}\) with \(y(0) = 3\).
Solve \(\frac{dy}{dx} = y^{2}\) with \(y(0) = 1\).

steps.title: Slope Fields
steps.mastery: Sketch and read a slope field for a differential equation.
steps.practice: Draw slope marks at 9 points with x and y in {-1, 0, 1} for dy/dx = x + y.
steps.detail: Each mark shows the slope a solution has at that point. Following the marks traces a solution curve.
steps.proof: 9 marks drawn, with slope 0 at (0, 0), (1, -1) and (-1, 1).
steps.pitfall: Drawing marks with the wrong sign in some quadrant.

problems.prompt: Slope of \(\frac{dy}{dx} = x + y\) at (1, 2)?
Where is \(\frac{dy}{dx} = x - y\) zero?
For \(\frac{dy}{dx} = y\), what do the slopes do as \(y\) grows?

steps.title: Exponential Growth
steps.mastery: Model growth or decay with the differential equation dy/dt = ky.
steps.practice: A culture of 500 bacteria doubles every 3 hours. Write P(t) and find P(9).
steps.detail: dy/dt = ky gives y = y0 e^(kt). A doubling time fixes k = ln 2/3. Half life works the same with decay.
steps.pitfall: Using the doubling time as k directly.

problems.prompt: Half life 5 years, start 80 g. Amount after 10 years?
Doubling time if \(k = \ln \frac{2}{4}\)?
\(y = 100e^{0.03t}\). Rate of growth at \(t = 0\)?

steps.title: Euler Method
steps.mastery: Approximate a solution step by step with tangent lines.
steps.practice: Use Euler method with step 0.5 to estimate y(1) for dy/dx = y with y(0) = 1.
steps.detail: Each step moves along the tangent line: y new = y + h f(x, y). Smaller steps give better estimates.
steps.pitfall: Using the slope at the end of a step instead of the start.

problems.prompt: One Euler step of 0.1 from \(y(0) = 2\) with \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 3\)?
Two Euler steps of 0.5 for \(\frac{dy}{dx} = x\) from \(y(0) = 0\)?
True \(y(1)\) for \(\frac{dy}{dx} = y\), \(y(0) = 1\), compared with the 2.25 estimate?
problems.answer: e is about 2.718, so Euler underestimates.

steps.title: Evaluate With FTC
steps.mastery: Compute a definite integral as F(b) - F(a).
steps.practice: Evaluate the integral of (3x^2 + 2x) from 1 to 3 using an antiderivative.
steps.detail: The fundamental theorem turns an area into a subtraction. Find any antiderivative, plug in the top and bottom and subtract.
steps.pitfall: Subtracting in the wrong order, F(a) - F(b).

problems.prompt: Integral of \(2x\) from 0 to 3?
Integral of \(\cos x\) from 0 to \(\frac{\pi}{2}\)?
Integral of \(e^{x}\) from 0 to \(\ln 3\)?

steps.title: Derivative of an Integral
steps.mastery: Differentiate a function defined as an integral.
steps.practice: Find the derivative of g(x) = integral of t^3 from 0 to x, and of h(x) = integral of t^3 from 0 to x^2.
steps.detail: The derivative of the integral up to x is the integrand at x. With x^2 as the top, the chain rule adds a factor of 2x.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting the chain rule when the upper limit is not x.

problems.prompt: \(\frac{d}{dx}\) of integral of \(\sin t\) from 1 to \(x\)?
\(\frac{d}{dx}\) of integral of \(t^{2}\) from 0 to \(3x\)?
\(\frac{d}{dx}\) of integral of \(e^{t}\) from \(x\) to 5?

steps.title: Accumulation Functions
steps.mastery: Read an accumulation function from a graph of its rate.
steps.practice: Given f is a line from (0, 2) to (4, -2), find g(4) where g(x) = integral of f from 0 to x.
steps.detail: g adds signed area as x moves right. Where f is positive g grows, and where f is negative it shrinks. g has a max where f crosses from + to -.
steps.proof: g(4) = 2 - 2 = 0, with g largest at x = 2.
steps.pitfall: Treating area below the axis as positive.

problems.prompt: \(f > 0\) on [0, 3]. Is g increasing there?
f changes from positive to negative at \(x = 5\), and g is the integral of f. What does g have at \(x = 5\)?
problems.answer: A local max, since \(g' = f\) goes from positive to negative there.

problems.prompt: \(g(x)\) = integral of f from 2 to \(x\). \(g(2)\)?

steps.title: Average Value
steps.mastery: Find the average value of a function on an interval.
steps.practice: Find the average value of f(x) = x^2 on [0, 3].
steps.detail: The average value is the integral divided by the length. It is the height of the rectangle with the same area.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting to divide by the length of the interval.

problems.prompt: Average value of \(2x\) on [0, 4]?
Average value of \(\sin x\) on [0, pi]?
Average value of 6 on [1, 10]?

steps.title: Total From a Table
steps.mastery: Estimate an integral from data with a trapezoid sum.
steps.practice: Estimate the integral of r(t) from 0 to 6 with a trapezoid sum using r(0) = 4, r(2) = 7, r(4) = 9, r(6) = 6.
steps.detail: AP problems often give tables instead of formulas. Trapezoids average the endpoints of each interval, and unequal widths must be handled separately.
steps.pitfall: Using equal widths when the table gaps differ.

problems.prompt: Trapezoid with heights 3 and 5 and width 2. Area?
Right Riemann sum for the same data on [0, 4]?

steps.title: Differentiate Both Sides
steps.mastery: Find dy/dx when y is mixed into an equation with x.
steps.practice: Find dy/dx for x^2 + y^2 = 25 by differentiating both sides with respect to x.
steps.detail: Treat y as a function of x, so every y term picks up a dy/dx from the chain rule. Then solve for dy/dx.
steps.proof: 2x + 2y dy/dx = 0, so dy/dx = -x/y.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting the dy/dx on the y terms.

problems.prompt: Derivative of \(y^{3}\) with respect to \(x\)?
Find \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) for \(xy = 6\).
Find \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) for \(x^{3} + y^{3} = 9\).

steps.title: Slope at a Point
steps.mastery: Plug a point into an implicit derivative to get a tangent slope.
steps.practice: Find the slope of x^2 + y^2 = 25 at (3, 4) and write the tangent line.
steps.detail: Implicit derivatives depend on both x and y. Substitute the point to get a number, then use point-slope form.
steps.proof: Slope -3/4 and tangent y = -3x/4 + 25/4.
steps.pitfall: Using only the x value of the point.

problems.prompt: Slope of \(xy = 12\) at (3, 4)?
Where does \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 16\) have a vertical tangent?

steps.title: Products With y
steps.mastery: Handle mixed terms where x and y are multiplied together.
steps.practice: Find dy/dx for x^2 y + y^3 = 10.
steps.detail: A term like x^2 y is a product, so it needs the product rule as well as the chain rule on y. Group the dy/dx terms before solving.
steps.pitfall: Differentiating xy as just y.

problems.prompt: Derivative of 3xy with respect to \(x\)?
Find \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) for \(xy^{2} = 8\).
Find \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) for \(e^{xy} = 5\).

steps.title: Second Derivatives Implicitly
steps.mastery: Find d^2y/dx^2 by differentiating dy/dx again.
steps.practice: Find d^2y/dx^2 for x^2 + y^2 = 25 starting from dy/dx = -x/y.
steps.detail: Differentiate the quotient -x/y, then replace dy/dx with -x/y and simplify. Using the original equation often cleans it up.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting that y in the answer still depends on x.

problems.prompt: \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) of \(y = x^{3}\) directly?
For \(y^{2} = x\), find \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).

steps.title: Inverse Function Derivatives
steps.mastery: Use implicit differentiation to find derivatives of inverse functions.
steps.practice: Derive the derivative of ln x by differentiating e^y = x implicitly.
steps.detail: Writing y = ln x as e^y = x and differentiating gives dy/dx = 1/e^y = 1/x. The same trick gives arcsin and arctan.
steps.proof: dy/dx = 1/x.
steps.pitfall: Memorizing inverse derivatives without seeing where they come from.

problems.prompt: Derivative of \(\arctan x\) at \(x = 1\)?
Derivative of \(\arcsin x\) at \(x = 0\)?
If \(f(2) = 5\) and f prime of 2 is 3, find the derivative of f inverse at 5.

steps.title: Area Under a Curve
steps.mastery: Estimate the area under a curve with rectangles.
steps.practice: Estimate the area under y = x^2 from 0 to 2 with 4 right endpoint rectangles.
steps.detail: Each rectangle has width 0.5 and height f at its right end. More rectangles give a better estimate, and the limit is the definite integral.
steps.pitfall: Using the wrong width when the interval is not length 1.

problems.prompt: Width of 4 rectangles on [0, 2]?
Left endpoint estimate for \(y = x^{2}\) on [0, 2] with 4 rectangles?
Exact area under \(y = x^{2}\) on [0, 2]?

steps.title: Antiderivatives
steps.mastery: Find a function whose derivative is the given one.
steps.practice: Find antiderivatives of x^4, 3x^2 - 2, 1/x and cos x, each with + C.
steps.detail: Reverse the power rule: raise the power by 1 and divide by the new power. The + C matters because every constant has derivative 0.
steps.proof: x^5/5, x^3 - 2x, ln|x| and sin x, each + C.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting + C on an indefinite integral.

problems.prompt: Antiderivative of \(6x\)?
Antiderivative of \(e^{x} + 1\)?
Antiderivative of \(\frac{1}{x^{3}}\)?

steps.title: Definite Integral Properties
steps.mastery: Use linearity and interval splitting to simplify integrals.
steps.practice: Given the integral of f from 0 to 5 is 8 and from 0 to 2 is 3, find the integral of f from 2 to 5 and of 4f from 0 to 5.
steps.detail: Integrals split over intervals and pull out constants. Swapping the limits flips the sign. These rules save work on AP style tables.
steps.proof: 5 and 32.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting that reversing the limits changes the sign.

problems.prompt: Integral of f from 5 to 0 if from 0 to 5 is 8?
Integral of \((f + 2)\) from 0 to 5 if the integral of f is 8?
Integral of any f from 3 to 3?

steps.title: Net Change
steps.mastery: Read a definite integral of a rate as total change.
steps.practice: Water flows in at r(t) = 3t liters per minute. Find how much enters from t = 0 to t = 4.
steps.detail: Integrating a rate gives the total change over the interval. Units are rate units times time units.
steps.proof: 24 liters.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting that negative parts of a rate subtract.

problems.prompt: Velocity 5 m/s for 10 s. Distance?
\(v(t) = 2t\) on [0, 3]. Displacement?
\(v(t) = t - 2\) on [0, 4]. Give the displacement, then the total distance.

steps.title: Area With Geometry
steps.mastery: Evaluate definite integrals by recognizing shapes.
steps.practice: Evaluate the integral of sqrt(9 - x^2) from -3 to 3 and of |x| from -2 to 2 using geometry.
steps.detail: Some integrals are areas of familiar shapes. A semicircle and 2 triangles need no antiderivative at all.
steps.proof: 9 pi/2 and 4.
steps.pitfall: Treating area below the x axis as positive in a definite integral.

problems.prompt: Integral of 4 from 1 to 6?
Integral of \(x\) from 0 to 4?
Integral of \(\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}\) from 0 to 2?
problems.answer: \(\pi\). It's a quarter of a circle of radius 2.

steps.title: Check the Form First
steps.mastery: Use L Hopital only on 0/0 or infinity/infinity forms.
steps.practice: Classify the forms of 3 limits as x approaches 0: sin x/x, (1 - cos x)/x and (x + 1)/x.
steps.detail: L Hopital works only for 0/0 and infinity over infinity. Using it on other forms gives wrong answers.
steps.proof: 0/0, 0/0 and 1/0, so only the first 2 qualify.
steps.pitfall: Applying L Hopital to a form like 1/0.

problems.prompt: Form of \(\frac{e^{x} - 1}{x}\) at 0?
Form of \(\frac{x^{2}}{e^{x}}\) at infinity?
Form of \(\frac{x + 2}{x - 1}\) at 1 from the right?
problems.answer: Not indeterminate. It's \(\frac{3}{0}\), so L'Hopital's rule doesn't apply and the limit is \(+ \infty\).

steps.title: Apply the Rule
steps.mastery: Differentiate top and bottom separately and take the limit again.
steps.practice: Evaluate the limits of sin x/x and (e^x - 1)/x as x approaches 0 with L Hopital.
steps.detail: Take the derivative of the top and of the bottom, not the quotient rule. Then try the limit again.
steps.proof: 1 and 1.
steps.pitfall: Using the quotient rule instead of separate derivatives.

problems.prompt: Limit of \(\frac{1 - \cos x}{x^{2}}\) at 0?
Limit of \(\ln \frac{x}{x - 1}\) at 1?
Limit of \(\frac{x}{e^{x}}\) as \(x\) goes to infinity?

steps.title: Apply It Twice
steps.mastery: Repeat L Hopital when the form stays indeterminate.
steps.practice: Evaluate the limit of x^2/e^x as x goes to infinity, applying the rule twice.
steps.detail: After 1 step you may still get infinity over infinity. Check the form each time before applying again.
steps.proof: 2x/e^x, then 2/e^x, so the limit is 0.
steps.pitfall: Applying again after the form is no longer indeterminate.

problems.prompt: Limit of \(\frac{e^{x} - 1 - x}{x^{2}}\) at 0?
Limit of \(\frac{x^{3}}{e^{x}}\) at infinity?
Limit of \(\frac{x - \sin x}{x^{3}}\) at 0?

steps.title: Other Indeterminate Forms
steps.mastery: Rewrite 0 times infinity and 1^infinity forms as quotients.
steps.practice: Evaluate the limit of x ln x as x approaches 0 from the right by rewriting it as ln x/(1/x).
steps.detail: Products become quotients, and powers become logs: take ln, find that limit, then exponentiate.
steps.proof: The limit is 0.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting to exponentiate at the end of a 1^infinity problem.

problems.prompt: Limit of \((1 + \frac{1}{x})^{x}\) as \(x\) goes to infinity?
Limit of \(xe^{-x}\) as \(x\) goes to infinity?
Limit of \(x^{x}\) as \(x\) approaches 0 from the right?

steps.title: Compare Growth Rates
steps.mastery: Rank logs, powers and exponentials by how fast they grow.
steps.practice: Rank ln x, x^0.1, x^5 and 2^x by growth using L Hopital on ratios.
steps.detail: Any exponential beats any power, and any power beats any log. These facts settle many limits at a glance.
steps.proof: ln x < x^0.1 < x^5 < 2^x for large x.
steps.pitfall: Assuming x^100 beats 1.01^x forever.

problems.prompt: Limit of \(\ln x/x\) at infinity?
Limit of \(\frac{x^{10}}{2^{x}}\) at infinity?
Which grows faster, \(x^{3}\) or \(e^{0.01x}\)?

steps.title: Limits by Substitution
steps.mastery: Find a limit by plugging in when the function is continuous there.
steps.practice: Evaluate the limits of x^2 + 3x, (x + 1)/(x - 2) and sqrt(x + 5) as x approaches 4.
steps.detail: If a function has no break at the point, the limit is just its value. Always try plugging in first, and only reach for algebra when you get 0/0.
steps.pitfall: Doing algebra on a limit that direct substitution already answers.

problems.prompt: Find the limit of \(3x - 1\) as \(x\) approaches 2.
Find the limit of \(x^{3} - 2x\) as \(x\) approaches -1.
Find the limit of \(\frac{x^{2} + 1}{x + 3}\) as \(x\) approaches 0.

steps.title: Factor and Cancel
steps.mastery: Resolve a 0/0 limit by factoring out the common term.
steps.practice: Evaluate the limit of (x^2 - 9)/(x - 3) as x approaches 3 by factoring.
steps.detail: A 0/0 result means a shared factor hides in the top and bottom. Cancel it, then substitute. The original function has a hole there, but the limit exists.
steps.proof: (x - 3)(x + 3)/(x - 3) = x + 3, so the limit is 6.
steps.pitfall: Writing the answer as 0/0 = 1 or 0.

problems.prompt: Limit of \(\frac{x^{2} - 4}{x - 2}\) as \(x\) approaches 2?
Limit of \(\frac{x^{2} - 5x + 6}{x - 2}\) as \(x\) approaches 2?
Limit of \(\frac{x^{3} - 8}{x - 2}\) as \(x\) approaches 2?

steps.title: Rationalize the Root
steps.mastery: Multiply by a conjugate to clear a square root from a 0/0 limit.
steps.practice: Evaluate the limit of (sqrt(x + 4) - 2)/x as x approaches 0 by multiplying by sqrt(x + 4) + 2.
steps.detail: The conjugate turns a difference of roots into a difference of squares, which cancels the troublesome factor.
steps.pitfall: Multiplying only the top by the conjugate.

problems.prompt: What is the conjugate of \(\sqrt{x} - 3\)?
Limit of \(\frac{\sqrt{x} - 3}{x - 9}\) as \(x\) approaches 9?
Limit of \(\frac{\sqrt{x + 1} - 1}{x}\) as \(x\) approaches 0?

steps.title: One-Sided Limits
steps.mastery: Check the left and right limits separately when a function jumps.
steps.practice: Find the left and right limits of |x|/x at 0 and decide if the full limit exists.
steps.detail: A limit exists only if both sides agree. Absolute values, piecewise functions and vertical asymptotes are where the sides often differ.
steps.proof: Left limit -1, right limit 1, so the limit does not exist.
steps.pitfall: Checking only one side.

problems.prompt: Limit of \(\frac{1}{x}\) as \(x\) approaches 0 from the right?
\(f(x) = x + 1\) for \(x < 2\) and 5 for \(x \ge 2\). Left and right limits at 2?
Does the limit of \(\frac{1}{x^{2}}\) as \(x\) approaches 0 exist as a number?
problems.answer: No, it grows to infinity from both sides.

steps.title: Limits at Infinity
steps.mastery: Find end behavior by comparing the highest powers.
steps.practice: Evaluate the limits of (3x^2 + 1)/(x^2 - 5), (2x + 7)/(x^2) and (x^3)/(4x^2) as x goes to infinity.
steps.detail: Divide by the highest power in the bottom. Equal degrees give the ratio of leading coefficients, a bigger bottom gives 0 and a bigger top grows without bound.
steps.proof: 3, 0 and infinity.
steps.pitfall: Plugging in infinity as if it were a number.

problems.prompt: Limit of \(\frac{5x}{2x + 1}\) as \(x\) goes to infinity?
Limit of \(\frac{7}{x + 3}\) as \(x\) goes to infinity?
Limit of \(\frac{4x^{3} - x}{2x^{3} + 9}\) as \(x\) goes to infinity?

steps.title: Tangent Line Approximation
steps.mastery: Replace a curve near a known point with the straight line that touches it.
steps.practice: Estimate sqrt(4.1) with the tangent line to sqrt(x) at x = 4.
steps.detail: L(x) = f(a) + f prime (a)(x - a) is close to f near a. It is the simplest useful approximation in calculus.
steps.pitfall: Using a point far from where the function is known.

problems.prompt: Linearize \(x^{2}\) at \(x = 3\).
Estimate \(3.01^{2}\) with that line.
Estimate cube root of 8.1 with the tangent at 8.

steps.title: Over or Under
steps.mastery: Use concavity to tell if a tangent estimate is too high or too low.
steps.practice: Check whether 2.025 overestimates sqrt(4.1) by looking at the sign of the second derivative of sqrt(x).
steps.detail: If f is concave down the tangent lies above the curve, so the estimate is too high. Concave up means too low.
steps.proof: sqrt(x) is concave down, so 2.025 is a little too high.
steps.pitfall: Guessing over or under without checking the second derivative.

problems.prompt: \(x^{2}\) is concave up. Is its tangent estimate high or low?
The tangent to \(\ln x\) at \(x = 1\) estimates \(\ln 1.1\) as 0.1. High or low?
problems.answer: High, since \(\ln x\) is concave down.

problems.prompt: Since \(e^{x}\) is concave up, is \(1 + x\) an over or under estimate of \(e^{0.2}\)?
problems.answer: Under, because the curve sits above its tangent.

steps.title: Differentials
steps.mastery: Use dy = f prime dx to estimate small changes.
steps.practice: A square side grows from 10 cm to 10.1 cm. Estimate the change in area with differentials.
steps.detail: dA = 2s ds = 2(10)(0.1). Differentials give quick estimates of how errors in input affect output.
steps.proof: About 2 cm^2.
steps.pitfall: Computing the exact change when an estimate is asked for.

problems.prompt: \(y = x^{3}\), \(x\) from 2 to 2.01. Estimate dy.
Circle radius 5 changes by 0.2. Estimate dA.
Exact change in area for the square from 10 to 10.1?

steps.title: Error Propagation
steps.mastery: Estimate how a measurement error affects a computed result.
steps.practice: A sphere radius is 10 cm with possible error 0.1 cm. Estimate the error in its volume.
steps.detail: dV = 4 pi r^2 dr. Relative error dV/V = 3 dr/r shows the volume error is 3 times the radius error in percent.
steps.proof: About 40 pi cm^3, or 3% relative error.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting that relative error multiplies by the power.

problems.prompt: Relative error 1% in radius. Relative error in area?
Relative error 2% in side. Relative error in cube volume?
dV for a cube with \(s = 5\) and ds = 0.1?

steps.title: Newton Method
steps.mastery: Find roots by repeated tangent lines.
steps.practice: Apply 2 steps of Newton method to x^2 - 2 = 0 starting at x = 1.
steps.detail: x new = x - f(x)/f prime (x). Each step uses the tangent root as the next guess, and it usually converges fast.
steps.pitfall: Starting where f prime is 0, which breaks the method.

problems.prompt: Newton step for \(x^{2} - 9\) from \(x = 4\)?
Newton formula for \(f(x) = x^{3} - 5\)?
Why does Newton method fail at a point where f prime = 0?
problems.answer: The tangent is flat and never crosses 0.

steps.title: Position, Velocity, Acceleration
steps.mastery: Move between position, velocity and acceleration with derivatives.
steps.practice: Given s(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t meters, find v(t), a(t) and when the particle is at rest.
steps.detail: Velocity is the derivative of position, and acceleration is the derivative of velocity. At rest means v = 0.
steps.proof: v = 3t^2 - 12t + 9, a = 6t - 12, at rest at t = 1 and t = 3.
steps.pitfall: Setting position to 0 to find when the particle is at rest.

problems.prompt: \(s(t) = 4t^{2}\). Velocity at \(t = 2\)?
\(v(t) = t^{2} - 4\). Acceleration at \(t = 3\)?
\(v(t) = t^{2} - 4\). When is the particle at rest for \(t \ge 0\)?

steps.title: Speeding Up or Slowing Down
steps.mastery: Compare the signs of velocity and acceleration.
steps.practice: Decide whether the particle with v = 3t^2 - 12t + 9 is speeding up at t = 2 and t = 4.
steps.detail: Speed increases when v and a have the same sign and decreases when they differ. This is a favorite AP free response question.
steps.proof: At t = 2, v = -3 and a = 0, so neither. At t = 4, v = 9 and a = 12, so speeding up.
steps.pitfall: Saying positive acceleration always means speeding up.

problems.prompt: \(v = - 5\) and \(a = - 2\). Speeding up or slowing down?
\(v = 0\) and \(a = 3\) at an instant. Is it about to move in the positive or negative direction?

steps.title: Displacement and Distance
steps.mastery: Integrate velocity for displacement and its absolute value for distance.
steps.practice: For v(t) = t - 3 on [0, 5], find the displacement and the total distance traveled.
steps.detail: Displacement is the integral of v. Distance is the integral of |v|, which requires splitting where v changes sign.
steps.proof: Displacement -2.5, total distance 4.5 + 2 = 6.5.
steps.pitfall: Reporting displacement when distance is asked.

problems.prompt: \(v(t) = 2\) on [0, 4]. Displacement?
\(v(t) = t - 1\) on [0, 2]. Total distance?
Start at \(x = 3\) with displacement -5. Final position?

steps.title: Position From Velocity
steps.mastery: Find position by adding the initial position to the integral of velocity.
steps.practice: A particle starts at x = 4 with v(t) = 2t + 1. Find x(3).
steps.detail: x(t) = x(0) + integral of v from 0 to t. Forgetting the starting position is the most common error.
steps.pitfall: Leaving out the initial position.

steps.title: Say the Units
steps.mastery: State units for each quantity in a motion problem.
steps.practice: Give units for s, v, a and the integral of v from 0 to 10 when s is in meters and t in seconds.
steps.detail: Position is m, velocity m/s, acceleration m/s^2 and the integral of velocity is m. AP graders take points for missing units.
steps.proof: m, m/s, m/s^2 and m.
steps.pitfall: Leaving units off a final answer.

problems.prompt: Units of the integral of \(a(t)\) in m/s² over seconds?
Units of dT/dt if T is in degrees and t in hours?
Units of the integral of \(r(t)\) from 0 to 5 if r is in liters per minute?

steps.title: State the Theorem
steps.mastery: Know the 2 conditions and the conclusion of the Mean Value Theorem.
steps.practice: Write the conditions of the Mean Value Theorem and check them for f(x) = x^2 on [1, 3].
steps.detail: f must be continuous on [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b). Then some c has f prime (c) equal to the average slope.
steps.proof: Both hold, and the average slope is 4.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting to check differentiability.

problems.prompt: Average slope of \(x^{2}\) on [1, 3]?
Does |x| on [-1, 1] satisfy the MVT conditions?
problems.answer: No, it is not differentiable at 0.

problems.prompt: Does \(x^{3}\) on [0, 2] satisfy the conditions?

steps.title: Find the c
steps.mastery: Solve f prime (c) = average slope for c.
steps.practice: Find c for f(x) = x^3 - x on [0, 2] guaranteed by the Mean Value Theorem.
steps.detail: Compute the average slope, set f prime (c) equal to it and keep only the c inside the interval.
steps.proof: Average slope 3, so 3c^2 - 1 = 3 and c = 2/sqrt(3).
steps.pitfall: Keeping a c outside the interval.

problems.prompt: c for \(\sqrt{x}\) on [0, 4]?
c for \(\frac{1}{x}\) on [1, 3]?

steps.title: Rolle Theorem
steps.mastery: Use the special case where f(a) = f(b).
steps.practice: Show f(x) = x^2 - 4x has a point with f prime = 0 on [0, 4] using Rolle theorem.
steps.detail: If f(a) = f(b) and f is smooth, the graph must turn somewhere, so f prime is 0 there.
steps.proof: f(0) = f(4) = 0, and f prime (2) = 0.
steps.pitfall: Using Rolle when f(a) and f(b) differ.

problems.prompt: \(f(1) = f(5) = 3\) and f is differentiable. What must happen?
c for \(\sin x\) on [0, pi] by Rolle?
Can a differentiable f have \(f(0) = f(2)\) and f prime never 0?

steps.title: Speed Trap Problems
steps.mastery: Apply MVT to average speed in a real setting.
steps.practice: A car travels 120 miles in 2 hours. Use the MVT to show it went exactly 60 mph at some moment.
steps.detail: Average velocity is the slope of the position graph. If position is smooth, the instant speed equals the average at some time.
steps.proof: Average speed 60 mph, so v(c) = 60 at some c.
steps.pitfall: Saying the car must have gone 60 mph the whole time.

problems.prompt: 90 miles in 1.5 hours. Speed guaranteed at some instant?
A toll booth 100 miles apart records 1.25 hours. Speed guaranteed?
Temperature rose 20 degrees in 4 hours. Rate guaranteed?

steps.title: Prove Inequalities With MVT
steps.mastery: Use MVT to bound how much a function can change.
steps.practice: Show |sin a - sin b| <= |a - b| for all a and b using the Mean Value Theorem.
steps.detail: MVT gives sin a - sin b = cos(c)(a - b), and |cos c| <= 1. Bounding the derivative bounds the change.
steps.proof: The bound follows from |cos c| <= 1.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting to take absolute values.

problems.prompt: If |f prime| <= 3 on [0, 5], how much can f change?
\(f(0) = 2\) and f prime <= 4. Largest \(f(3)\)?
Show \(e^{x} \ge 1 + x\) for \(x > 0\).
problems.answer: By the mean value theorem on [0, x], \(\frac{e^{x} - 1}{x} = e^{c}\) for some c in (0, x). Since \(c > 0\), \(e^{c} > 1\), so \(e^{x} - 1 > x\).

steps.title: Find Critical Points
steps.mastery: Locate where the derivative is 0 or undefined.
steps.practice: Find the critical points of f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 1 and classify each with the first derivative test.
steps.detail: Max and min values happen at critical points or endpoints. Checking the sign of f prime on each side says whether a point is a max, a min or neither.
steps.proof: x = 1 is a local max and x = 3 is a local min.
steps.pitfall: Calling every critical point a maximum.

problems.prompt: Critical point of \(x^{2} - 8x\)?
Critical points of \(x^{3} - 3x\)?
Is \(x = 0\) a max, min or neither for \(x^{3}\)?

steps.title: Closed Interval Method
steps.mastery: Find the absolute max and min on a closed interval.
steps.practice: Find the absolute max and min of f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 1 on [0, 5].
steps.detail: Check every critical point inside the interval and both endpoints, then compare the values. The biggest is the max and the smallest is the min.
steps.proof: Min -3 at x = 2, max 6 at x = 5.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting to check the endpoints.

problems.prompt: Max of \(\sin x\) on [0, pi]?

steps.title: Build the Model
steps.mastery: Turn a word problem into one function of one variable.
steps.practice: A farmer has 200 m of fence for a rectangle against a barn. Write the area as a function of 1 side.
steps.detail: Name the quantity to optimize, write it with 2 variables, then use the constraint to remove 1. The modeling step is usually harder than the calculus.
steps.proof: A(x) = x(200 - 2x), with x the side perpendicular to the barn.
steps.pitfall: Starting to differentiate before the function has 1 variable.

problems.prompt: Rectangle with perimeter 40. Area as a function of width w?
Box with square base side \(x\) and volume 32. Height?
Two numbers sum to 50. Product as a function of \(x\)?

steps.title: Solve the Optimization
steps.mastery: Finish an optimization and check it is a max or min.
steps.practice: Maximize A(x) = x(200 - 2x) and state the dimensions of the pen.
steps.detail: Set the derivative to 0, solve and confirm with the second derivative or endpoints. Then answer the question that was asked, with units.
steps.proof: x = 50 m, giving a 50 m by 100 m pen with area 5000 m^2.
steps.pitfall: Stopping at x and not giving the dimensions asked for.

problems.prompt: What is the maximum value of \(x(20 - x)\)?
What is the minimum value of \(x + \frac{16}{x}\) for \(x > 0\)?
Open box from a 12 by 12 sheet with corners \(x\) cut out. Best \(x\)?

steps.title: Distance and Cost Problems
steps.mastery: Optimize distances and costs with a square root or a sum.
steps.practice: Find the point on y = x^2 closest to (0, 2) by minimizing the squared distance.
steps.detail: Minimizing the squared distance avoids a messy root and has the same minimum point. This trick works for any closest point problem.
steps.proof: Points (sqrt(3/2), 3/2) and (-sqrt(3/2), 3/2).
steps.pitfall: Differentiating the square root form and making algebra errors.

problems.prompt: Squared distance from \((x, x^{2})\) to (0, 2)?
Closest point on \(y = 2x\) to (5, 0)?
Point on \(x + y = 4\) closest to the origin?

steps.title: Parametric Slope
steps.mastery: Find dy/dx for a curve given by x(t) and y(t).
steps.practice: Find dy/dx for x = t^2, y = t^3 at t = 2.
steps.detail: dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt). Find both derivatives in t, divide and substitute the parameter value.
steps.pitfall: Dividing dx/dt by dy/dt, upside down.

problems.prompt: \(x = \cos t\), \(y = \sin t\). \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) at \(t = \frac{\pi}{4}\)?
Where does \(x = t^{2}\), \(y = t^{3} - 3t\) have a horizontal tangent?

steps.title: Parametric Arc Length
steps.mastery: Compute arc length as the integral of sqrt((dx/dt)^2 + (dy/dt)^2).
steps.practice: Find the length of x = 3cos t, y = 3sin t for t from 0 to 2 pi.
steps.detail: The integrand is the speed along the curve. A circle of radius 3 makes a good check, since the answer is its circumference.
steps.proof: 6 pi.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting the square root around the sum.

problems.prompt: Speed for \(x = 3t\), \(y = 4t\)?
Length of \(x = 3t\), \(y = 4t\) for t from 0 to 2?
Length of \(x = t\), \(y = (\frac{2}{3})t^{\frac{3}{2}}\) from 0 to 3?

steps.title: Vector Motion
steps.mastery: Find velocity, speed and acceleration of a particle in the plane.
steps.practice: For r(t) = (t^2, 2t), find the velocity, speed and acceleration at t = 1.
steps.detail: Differentiate each component. Speed is the length of the velocity vector, a single nonnegative number.
steps.proof: Velocity (2, 2), speed 2 sqrt(2), acceleration (2, 0).
steps.pitfall: Giving speed as a vector.

problems.prompt: Speed at \(t = 2\) for that path?
\(r(t) = (\cos t, \sin t)\). Acceleration at \(t = 0\)?

steps.title: Polar Area
steps.mastery: Compute area in polar form with (1/2) integral of r^2.
steps.practice: Find the area inside r = 2cos(theta) for theta from -pi/2 to pi/2.
steps.detail: Polar area adds thin wedges of area (1/2)r^2 d theta. This curve is a circle of radius 1, which checks the answer.
steps.proof: pi.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting the 1/2 or the square on r.

problems.prompt: Area inside \(r = 3\) for a full turn?
Area of \(r = \theta\) from 0 to pi?
Area of 1 petal of \(r = \cos (2\theta)\)?

steps.title: Polar Slopes
steps.mastery: Find dy/dx for a polar curve with x = r cos theta and y = r sin theta.
steps.practice: Find dy/dx for r = 1 + cos(theta) at theta = pi/2.
steps.detail: Write x and y in terms of theta, then use the parametric slope formula with theta as the parameter.
steps.proof: dy/dx = 1 at theta = pi/2.
steps.pitfall: Using dr/d(theta) as the slope.

problems.prompt: \(x\) and \(y\) for \(r = 2\) at \(\theta = 0\)?
\(\frac{dy}{dx}\) for \(r = 2\) at \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}\)?
Where does \(r = 2\sin (\theta)\) pass through the origin?

steps.title: Write the Relationship
steps.mastery: Connect the changing quantities with one equation before differentiating.
steps.practice: A 10 ft ladder slides down a wall. Write the equation linking its base distance x and height y.
steps.detail: Draw the picture, label what changes and write the equation that always holds. Only then differentiate with respect to time.
steps.pitfall: Plugging in numbers before differentiating, which freezes the variables.

problems.prompt: A circle with radius r. Area equation?
A cube with side s. Volume equation?
A cone with height h and radius \(\frac{h}{2}\). Volume?

steps.title: Differentiate in Time
steps.mastery: Take d/dt of each side so every changing value gets its own rate.
steps.practice: Differentiate x^2 + y^2 = 100 with respect to t and solve for dy/dt.
steps.detail: Each variable picks up its own rate, like dx/dt. Solve for the rate you want only after differentiating.
steps.proof: dy/dt = -(x/y) dx/dt.
steps.pitfall: Treating x or y as a constant.

steps.title: Ladder Problem
steps.mastery: Solve the classic sliding ladder rate problem.
steps.practice: Find how fast the top of the 10 ft ladder slides when its base, moving out at 2 ft/s, is 6 ft from the wall.
steps.detail: At x = 6 the height is 8, then substitute into dy/dt = -(x/y) dx/dt. The negative sign means the top moves down.
steps.proof: -1.5 ft/s, so the top slides down at 1.5 ft/s.
steps.pitfall: Using the height before finding it from the equation.

problems.prompt: Height of the 10 ft ladder when \(x = 8\)?
\(\frac{dy}{dt}\) when \(x = 8\) and \(\frac{dx}{dt} = 2\)?
A 13 ft ladder, base 5 ft out moving at 1 ft/s. \(\frac{dy}{dt}\)?

steps.title: Expanding Shapes
steps.mastery: Find rates for growing circles, spheres and cubes.
steps.practice: A balloon radius grows at 2 cm/s. Find how fast its volume grows when r = 5 cm.
steps.detail: dV/dt = 4 pi r^2 dr/dt. Substitute the radius at that instant only after differentiating.
steps.proof: 200 pi cm^3/s.
steps.pitfall: Substituting r = 5 into V before differentiating.

problems.prompt: Circle radius grows at 3 cm/s. \(\frac{dA}{dt}\) when \(r = 4\)?
Cube side grows at 1 cm/s. \(\frac{dV}{dt}\) when \(s = 3\)?
Sphere volume grows at 100 cm³/s. dr/dt when \(r = 5\)?

steps.title: Cones and Shadows
steps.mastery: Use similar triangles to remove an extra variable.
steps.practice: Water fills a cone 10 m tall with radius 5 m at 2 m^3/min. Find dh/dt when h = 4 m.
steps.detail: Similar triangles give r = h/2, so V = pi h^3/12. With 1 variable left, differentiate and solve.
steps.proof: dh/dt = 2/(4 pi) = 1/(2 pi) m/min.
steps.pitfall: Keeping both r and h and having 2 unknown rates.

problems.prompt: Cone with height 6 and radius 3. r in terms of h?
\(\frac{dV}{dt}\) for \(V = \pi \frac{h^{3}}{12}\)?
A 6 ft person walks away from a 15 ft lamp at 4 ft/s. Shadow length rate?

steps.title: Product Rule
steps.mastery: Differentiate a product as f prime g plus f g prime.
steps.practice: Differentiate x^2 sin x and (3x + 1)(x^2 - 4) with the product rule.
steps.detail: The derivative of a product is not the product of derivatives. Each factor takes a turn being differentiated while the other waits.
steps.pitfall: Multiplying the 2 derivatives together.

problems.prompt: Derivative of \(xe^{x}\)?
Derivative of \(x^{3}\ln x\)?
Derivative of \((x^{2} + 1)(x^{3} - x)\) at \(x = 1\)?

steps.title: Quotient Rule
steps.mastery: Differentiate a fraction with low d-high minus high d-low over low squared.
steps.practice: Differentiate (x^2 + 1)/(x - 3) with the quotient rule.
steps.detail: The order matters because of the minus sign. Simplifying the top afterward often reveals where the derivative is 0.
steps.pitfall: Swapping the order in the numerator, which flips the sign.

problems.prompt: Derivative of \(\frac{1}{x}\) using the quotient rule?
Derivative of \(\frac{x}{x + 1}\)?
Derivative of \(\sin x/x\) at \(x = \pi\)?

steps.title: Chain Rule
steps.mastery: Differentiate a function of a function as outside derivative times inside derivative.
steps.practice: Differentiate (3x^2 + 1)^5, sin(4x) and e^(x^2) with the chain rule.
steps.detail: Work from the outside in: differentiate the outer layer, keep the inside as is, then multiply by the derivative of the inside.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting to multiply by the derivative of the inside.

problems.prompt: Derivative of \((2x + 1)^{3}\)?
Derivative of \(\cos (x^{2})\)?
Derivative of \(\ln (5x^{3} + 2)\)?

steps.title: Trig and Exponential Rules
steps.mastery: Know the derivatives of sin, cos, tan, e^x and ln x by heart.
steps.practice: Write the derivatives of sin x, cos x, tan x, e^x, ln x and 2^x from memory, then check 3 with the definition.
steps.detail: These 6 come up in nearly every problem. Mixing up the sign of cos is the most common slip, so say it as cos goes to negative sin.
steps.proof: cos x, -sin x, sec^2 x, e^x, 1/x and 2^x ln 2.
steps.pitfall: Writing the derivative of cos x as sin x.

problems.prompt: Derivative of \(\tan x\) at \(x = 0\)?
Derivative of \(3^{x}\)?
Derivative of \(e^{3x}\sin x\)?

steps.title: Combine the Rules
steps.mastery: Choose and stack rules for a complicated expression.
steps.practice: Differentiate x^2 e^(3x)/(x + 1) by naming each rule before you apply it.
steps.detail: Big expressions are layers of products, quotients and chains. Naming the outermost structure first keeps the work organized.
steps.proof: Quotient rule outside, product and chain inside, with the derivative written in full.
steps.pitfall: Starting in the middle of the expression and losing a factor.

problems.prompt: Which rule comes first for \(\sin (x^{2})e^{x}\)?
problems.answer: The product rule, for \(\sin (x^{2})\) times \(e^{x}\). The chain rule comes inside it, for \(\sin (x^{2})\).

problems.prompt: Derivative of \(\sqrt{x^{2} + 9}\) at \(x = 4\)?
Derivative of \((\frac{x}{x + 1})^{2}\)?

steps.title: Geometric Series Test
steps.mastery: Sum a geometric series and check that |r| < 1.
steps.practice: Find the sums of the series 3(1/2)^n and 5(-1/3)^n from n = 0, or show they diverge.
steps.detail: A geometric series converges exactly when |r| < 1, to a/(1 - r). It is the series every test compares against.
steps.pitfall: Using the formula when |r| >= 1.

problems.prompt: Does the sum of \(2^{n}\) converge?

steps.title: Divergence Test
steps.mastery: Rule out convergence when the terms do not go to 0.
steps.practice: Apply the nth term test to n/(n + 1), 1/n and (-1)^n.
steps.detail: If the terms do not approach 0, the series diverges. If they do approach 0, the test says nothing, as 1/n shows.
steps.proof: n/(n + 1) and (-1)^n diverge. 1/n is inconclusive by this test.
steps.pitfall: Concluding convergence because the terms go to 0.

problems.prompt: Terms \(\frac{3n}{n + 2}\). Series converge?
Terms \(\frac{1}{n^{2}}\). Does the divergence test decide?
Terms \(\cos (\frac{1}{n})\). Series converge?

steps.title: p-Series and Comparison
steps.mastery: Judge a series by comparing it with 1/n^p, which converges only when p > 1.
steps.practice: Decide convergence of 1/n^2, 1/sqrt(n) and 1/(n^2 + 5) using p-series and comparison.
steps.detail: The sum of 1/n^p converges when p > 1. Comparing a messy series to a p-series settles most AP questions.
steps.proof: 1/n^2 converges, 1/sqrt(n) diverges and 1/(n^2 + 5) converges by comparison with 1/n^2.
steps.pitfall: Comparing in the wrong direction, which proves nothing.

problems.prompt: Does the sum of \(\frac{1}{n^{3}}\) converge?
Does the sum of \(\frac{1}{n}\) converge?
Does the sum of \(\frac{1}{n^{1.5} + 1}\) converge?

steps.title: Ratio Test
steps.mastery: Use the ratio of consecutive terms for factorials and powers.
steps.practice: Apply the ratio test to 2^n/n! and n^2/3^n.
steps.detail: If the limit of |a(n + 1)/a(n)| is below 1 the series converges, above 1 it diverges and equal to 1 tells nothing.
steps.proof: Ratios go to 0 and 1/3, so both converge.
steps.pitfall: Using the ratio test on p-series, where the ratio is always 1.

problems.prompt: Ratio limit for \(\frac{1}{n}\)!?
Ratio limit for \(\frac{2^{n}}{n \cdot 5^{n}}\)?
problems.answer: \(\frac{2}{5}\), since the ratio is \((\frac{2}{5}) \cdot \frac{n}{n + 1}\). It's below 1, so the series converges.

problems.prompt: Ratio limit for \(\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\)?

steps.title: Alternating Series
steps.mastery: Test alternating series and bound their error.
steps.practice: Show the sum of (-1)^(n + 1)/n converges and bound the error after 10 terms.
steps.detail: If the terms shrink to 0 and alternate, the series converges, and the error is less than the first term left out.
steps.proof: Converges, with error less than 1/11.
steps.pitfall: Using the alternating test when the terms do not decrease.

problems.prompt: Does the sum of \(\frac{(-1)^{n}}{n^{2}}\) converge?
Error bound after 4 terms of \(\frac{(-1)^{n + 1}}{n}\)?
problems.answer: Less than \(\frac{1}{5}\), the size of the 5th term.

problems.prompt: Does \((-1)^{n}\frac{n}{n + 1}\) converge?
problems.answer: No, the terms do not go to 0.

steps.title: Build a Taylor Polynomial
steps.mastery: Write the polynomial that matches a function and its derivatives at a point.
steps.practice: Write the 3rd degree Taylor polynomial of e^x at 0 and use it to estimate e^0.1.
steps.detail: Each term is f^(n)(a)(x - a)^n/n!. Near the center the polynomial is very close to the function.
steps.proof: 1 + x + x^2/2 + x^3/6, giving about 1.10517.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting the factorials in the denominators.

problems.prompt: 2nd degree Taylor polynomial of \(e^{x}\) at 0?
3rd degree Maclaurin polynomial of \(\sin x\)?
2nd degree Taylor polynomial of \(\ln x\) at 1?

steps.title: Know the Big Four
steps.mastery: Recall the Maclaurin series of e^x, sin x, cos x and 1/(1 - x).
steps.practice: Write the first 4 nonzero terms of e^x, sin x, cos x and 1/(1 - x) from memory.
steps.detail: These 4 series generate many others by substitution, multiplication or differentiation. Knowing them cold is required on the AP BC exam.
steps.pitfall: Mixing up which of sin and cos has the odd powers.

problems.prompt: First 3 terms of \(\cos x\)?
Series for \(\frac{1}{1 - x}\) for \(|x| < 1\)?
Coefficient of \(x^{5}\) in \(\sin x\)?

steps.title: New Series From Old
steps.mastery: Build series by substituting into known ones.
steps.practice: Find the Maclaurin series of e^(-x^2) and of 1/(1 + x^2) from known series.
steps.detail: Replace x with -x^2 in e^x, and x with -x^2 in 1/(1 - x). Integrating 1/(1 + x^2) term by term gives arctan.
steps.pitfall: Substituting into only the first term.

problems.prompt: Series for \(e^{2x}\), first 3 terms?
Series for \(x\sin x\), first 2 terms?
Series for \(\arctan x\), first 3 terms?

steps.title: Radius of Convergence
steps.mastery: Find where a power series converges with the ratio test.
steps.practice: Find the radius and interval of convergence of the sum of x^n/n.
steps.detail: The ratio test gives |x| < 1, so the radius is 1. Then test the endpoints separately: x = 1 diverges and x = -1 converges.
steps.proof: Radius 1, interval [-1, 1).
steps.pitfall: Forgetting to check the endpoints.

problems.prompt: Radius of the sum of \(x^{n}\)?
Radius of the sum of \(\frac{x^{n}}{n}\)!?
Radius of the sum of \(\frac{(x - 2)^{n}}{3^{n}}\)?

steps.title: Error Bounds
steps.mastery: Bound the error of a Taylor approximation.
steps.practice: Bound the error when cos(0.2) is approximated by 1 - x^2/2 using the alternating series bound.
steps.detail: For alternating series the error is less than the next term. The Lagrange bound uses the max of the next derivative for any series.
steps.proof: Error less than 0.2^4/24 = 0.0000667.
steps.pitfall: Using the term already included as the error bound.

problems.prompt: Next term after \(1 - \frac{x^{2}}{2}\) in \(\cos x\)?
Error bound for \(e^{0.1}\) using \(1 + x\)?
How many terms of \(\sin x\) give \(\sin (0.5)\) to within 0.001?

steps.title: U-Substitution
steps.mastery: Undo the chain rule by substituting the inside function.
steps.practice: Evaluate the integral of 2x(x^2 + 1)^5 dx with u = x^2 + 1.
steps.detail: Look for an inside function whose derivative also appears. Substitute u, change dx and integrate in u, then substitute back.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting to change dx to du.

problems.prompt: Integral of \(\cos (3x)dx\)?
Integral of \(xe^{x^{2}}dx\)?
Integral of \(\frac{x}{x^{2} + 4}dx\)?

steps.title: Change the Limits
steps.mastery: Change the bounds when substituting in a definite integral.
steps.practice: Evaluate the integral of 3x^2 sqrt(x^3 + 1) from 0 to 2 by changing the limits to u values.
steps.detail: With u = x^3 + 1, x = 0 gives u = 1 and x = 2 gives u = 9. Then you never need to switch back to x.
steps.pitfall: Using the old x limits with the new u integrand.

problems.prompt: With \(u = 2x + 1\), what are the new lower and upper limits for \(x\) from 0 to 1?
Integral of \(\frac{2x}{x^{2} + 1}\) from 0 to 1?
Integral of \(\sin x\cos x\) from 0 to \(\frac{\pi}{2}\)?

steps.title: Integration by Parts
steps.mastery: Integrate a product with u dv = uv - v du.
steps.practice: Evaluate the integral of x e^x dx and of x cos x dx by parts.
steps.detail: Choose u to get simpler when differentiated, often the polynomial. Logs go in u because their derivative is simpler.
steps.proof: x e^x - e^x + C and x sin x + cos x + C.
steps.pitfall: Choosing u so the new integral is harder than the first.

problems.prompt: For the integral of \(x^{2}\ln xdx\), which factor is u?
Integral of \(\ln x\) from 1 to \(e^{2}\)?
Integral of \(x^{2}e^{x}dx\)?

steps.title: Partial Fractions
steps.mastery: Split a rational function into simpler fractions before integrating.
steps.practice: Evaluate the integral of 1/((x - 1)(x + 2)) dx with partial fractions.
steps.detail: Write 1/((x - 1)(x + 2)) = A/(x - 1) + B/(x + 2), find A and B, then integrate each as a log.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting to do long division first when the top degree is too high.

problems.prompt: Decompose \(\frac{1}{x(x + 1)}\).
Integral of \(\frac{1}{x^{2} - 1}dx\)?
Decompose \(\frac{3x + 5}{(x + 1)(x + 2)}\).

steps.title: Pick the Technique
steps.mastery: Choose substitution, parts or partial fractions by the shape of the integrand.
steps.practice: Sort 10 integrals by technique, then solve 4 of them, 1 per technique plus 1 with 2 techniques.
steps.detail: An inside function with its derivative means substitution, a product of unlike types means parts, and a factorable rational function means partial fractions.
steps.proof: 10 integrals sorted and 4 solved.
steps.pitfall: Trying parts on every integral.

problems.prompt: Integral of \(x\sin (x^{2})\). Technique?
Integral of \(x\sin x\). Technique?
Integral of \(\frac{5}{(x - 2)(x + 3)}\). Technique?

steps.title: Graphics Transformations
steps.mastery: Move and rotate shapes in graphics with matrices.
steps.practice: Rotate the triangle (0, 0), (2, 0), (0, 1) by 90 degrees and scale it by 2 with 1 combined matrix.
steps.detail: Graphics engines combine many transformations into one matrix and apply it to every vertex. Homogeneous coordinates add translation.
steps.proof: Combined matrix [[0, -2], [2, 0]], giving (0, 0), (0, 4) and (-2, 0).
steps.pitfall: Applying the steps in the wrong order.

problems.prompt: Image of (1, 0) under a 90 degree rotation?
Why add a 3rd coordinate of 1 in 2D graphics?
problems.answer: So translations can be written as matrices.

problems.prompt: Matrix to scale \(x\) by 3 and \(y\) by 2?

steps.title: Ranking With Eigenvectors
steps.mastery: Rank pages or teams with the top eigenvector of a link matrix.
steps.practice: Find the steady state of the 3 page link matrix [[0, 0.5, 0.5], [0.5, 0, 0.5], [0.5, 0.5, 0]] by power iteration.
steps.detail: PageRank is the eigenvector for eigenvalue 1 of a link matrix. Power iteration finds it by repeated multiplication.
steps.proof: (1/3, 1/3, 1/3), all equal by symmetry.
steps.pitfall: Stopping power iteration after 1 step.

problems.prompt: What 2 steps does power iteration repeat?
problems.answer: Multiplying a vector by the matrix and normalizing.

problems.prompt: Largest eigenvalue of a 3 by 3 column stochastic matrix?
A page with 50 incoming links versus 2. Which usually ranks higher?

steps.title: Neural Network Layers
steps.mastery: Read a neural network layer as a matrix times a vector plus a bias.
steps.practice: Compute W x + b for W = [[1, -1], [2, 0]], x = (3, 1) and b = (0, 1), then apply ReLU.
steps.detail: A layer is a linear map followed by a simple nonlinearity. Training adjusts the matrix entries.
steps.proof: W x + b = (2, 7), and ReLU keeps (2, 7).
steps.pitfall: Forgetting the bias vector.

problems.prompt: ReLU of (-3, 4)?
Shape of W mapping 784 inputs to 128 outputs?
Number of weights in a 128 by 784 W?

steps.title: Compression
steps.mastery: Compress data with low rank approximations.
steps.practice: Estimate the storage saved by a rank 50 approximation of a 1000 by 800 matrix.
steps.detail: A rank k approximation stores k(m + n + 1) numbers. When the data has structure, a small k keeps most of the information.
steps.proof: 50 x 1801 = 90,050 numbers instead of 800,000.
steps.pitfall: Choosing k without checking how much detail is lost.

problems.prompt: Original entries in a 1000 by 800 matrix?
Storage for rank 10 of a 100 by 100 matrix?
Rank 1 storage for a 4 by 5 matrix?

steps.title: Quantum States as Vectors
steps.mastery: Represent a qubit as a unit vector and a gate as a matrix.
steps.practice: Apply the Hadamard matrix (1/sqrt(2))[[1, 1], [1, -1]] to (1, 0) and find the probabilities of each outcome.
steps.detail: A qubit is a unit vector, gates are orthogonal or unitary matrices, and probabilities are squared components.
steps.proof: (1/sqrt(2), 1/sqrt(2)), with probability 1/2 each.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting to square the components to get probabilities.

problems.prompt: Probability of outcome 0 for state (0.6, 0.8)?
Hadamard applied twice to (1, 0)?
Is (0.6, 0.8) a valid qubit state?

steps.title: Standard Basis
steps.mastery: Write any vector using the standard basis e1, e2, e3.
steps.practice: Write (4, -2, 5) as a combination of e1 = (1, 0, 0), e2 = (0, 1, 0) and e3 = (0, 0, 1).
steps.detail: In the standard basis, the components are the weights. This is why coordinates seem automatic.
steps.pitfall: Forgetting that coordinates depend on the basis chosen.

problems.prompt: Write (3, 7) using e1 and e2.
Write the standard basis vector e3 of 4D space.
Coordinates of e2 in the standard basis of 3D?

steps.title: Is It a Basis
steps.mastery: Check that a set spans the space and is independent.
steps.practice: Decide whether (1, 1) and (1, -1) form a basis for 2D space.
steps.detail: A basis needs the right number of independent vectors. In 2D, 2 independent vectors always span the plane.
steps.proof: Yes, they are independent and there are 2 of them.
steps.pitfall: Accepting 3 vectors as a basis for 2D space.

problems.prompt: Is {(1, 2), (2, 4)} a basis of 2D?
Is {(2, 0), (0, 5)} a basis of 2D?

steps.title: Coordinates in a New Basis
steps.mastery: Find the weights of a vector in a non standard basis.
steps.practice: Find the coordinates of (5, 1) in the basis (1, 1) and (1, -1).
steps.detail: Solve a(1, 1) + b(1, -1) = (5, 1). The same point has different coordinates in different bases.
steps.proof: a = 3 and b = 2.
